sentences.text: The station communications design separates supervisory requests, bay-level execution, and protection action so loss of one layer does not silently substitute for another.
Station Gateway brokers authorized station traffic across control-room and bay networks, applying configured protocol mappings, addressing, and access controls.
It rejects malformed, stale, or unauthorized requests and records each rejection with enough context for operations review.
Station Supervisory Control System presents available controls and indications to authorized operating personnel.
Control Room Operator issues state-changing requests only through approved operating procedures and the configured supervisory interface.
Bay Automation Controller validates each received request against local mode, interlocks, command authority, and equipment availability before issuing bay-level outputs.
Breaker Control Unit applies accepted output commands at the breaker interface and returns the resulting position and circuit-health indications.
Bay Automation Controller compares returned indications with the requested state and identifies incomplete or contradictory operation.
Bay Automation Controller uses the inspection tag to associate the applicable equipment context with an authorized record.
Station Gateway carries updated indications through the station interface using configured quality and timestamp attributes.
Station Supervisory Control System displays indication quality and stale-data status so operators can distinguish a current value from a retained value.
Sequence Event Archive retains time-tagged changes and control outcomes for event reconstruction and operational review.
Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time reference used to align event timestamps, subject to configured quality checks.
Bay Automation Controller monitors communication health and places affected points in a defined degraded state when updates exceed configured age limits.
Station Gateway reports link condition and protocol errors without converting a communication failure into an equipment-state change.
Tandem evaluates electrical quantities against approved settings and issues protective trip outputs without relying on supervisory communications.
North Protection Panel applies its assigned zone logic and maintains trip paths independently of supervisory network availability.
Transformer Protection Panel applies its assigned protective logic and reports abnormal protection conditions through its configured interface.
North Bay Controller maintains local bay control within the approved operating mode when supervisory communications are interrupted.
South Bay Controller reports local mode and control availability through its configured bay interface.
Engineering Workstation supports approved configuration review and does not serve as a routine source of operating commands.
Maintenance Remote Terminal access is restricted to authorized maintenance sessions and is not used to bypass local interlocks.
Station DC System supports control and protection functions through monitored station supply circuits, and supply loss is indicated as an abnormal station condition.
Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection event records and verifies that approved settings remain consistent with coordination requirements.
Substation Supervisor ensures communication changes, point mapping changes, and control logic changes are managed through station change control.
Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
